purpose: Milestone 2 asks for crash tests at every durable transition. A per-module sweep was completed first and found all ten modules with runtime transitions crossed by a kill. This is the finer enumeration that sweep said was needed: one row per commit and per fsync.
what_this_settles: The denominator. Thirty-one durable writes on runtime paths across twenty-two functions, and twelve more inside schema migrations. Before this the box's scope was a guess.
what_this_does_not_settle: The numerator, and static reading cannot supply it. Deciding which of the thirty-one a given kill fixture crosses means following calls through test helpers and through internal journal functions; an attempt to extract it by regex found nothing for one fixture that plainly does durable work, because its calls go through helpers. Reading each by hand would produce a number nobody could check, which is the same failure as counting test names.\n\n

instrument.where: journal::durable, behind the test-support feature rather than cfg(test), because the crash fixtures are integration tests and link the library without cfg(test) set.
instrument.how: Each durable site calls durable::record("module::function::detail") immediately after its commit or fsync. A crash fixture writes durable::reached() beside its ready signal, before being killed, and the parent asserts on that set.
instrument.proven_on: preparation.rs, all five runtime sites. The fixture now asserts it crossed enqueue_preparing_replacement and claim_preparation, and that complete_preparation is reached in exactly one of its two phases.
instrument.discrimination_check: Asserting a site name that does not exist fails with the measured set printed: ["preparation::claim_preparation", "preparation::enqueue_preparing_replacement"]. The assertion reads what the program did.
instrument.remaining: 26 of the 31 runtime sites are not yet instrumented. Mechanical: one line per site, one assertion per fixture.

measured_coverage.method: Every one of the 31 runtime sites now calls durable::record. Each crash fixture's child was run once per phase, its reached set read from disk, and the union taken. This is what the program did, not what a call graph says it would do. All eight crash fixtures now report, including the two older ones.
measured_coverage.reading_the_gap: prune_uploaded_payload is the last. It runs from collect_uploaded_payloads, not from the retired-working collector the handoff fixture used. Calling the right collector was tried and still does not reach it: that fixture leaves nothing prunable. Reaching it needs a fixture that uploads a payload, has its namespace go clean, and then collects -- and then crashes. The call was kept, asserting zero, because a collector run against a handed-off object is a state it has to tolerate.
measured_coverage.honest_status: 30 of 31. One remains, and what it needs is specific: an uploaded payload whose namespace has gone clean, collected, then a crash.

evidence_kinds.in_a_killed_child: 28 sites, read from the set each crash fixture persists before dying.
evidence_kinds.in_the_recovering_parent: 1 site, preparation::recover_preparation_files. Recovery runs in the process that opens the journal after the crash, so the parent asserts on its own reached set. The child now calls reserve_preparation before dying, which leaves the .cirrove-preparing- temporary that recovery exists to clean up.
